data.narrative:
Teradar is a Series B defense and security company founded by MIT-trained leadership (CEO Matt Carey) and deep technical expertise in terahertz sensing (CTO Gregory Charvat, ex-Humatics). The company has raised $175M to date. The comparable universe consists of 10 peers across Defense & Security—2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Castelion, and Defense Unicorns.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B progression, yielding $332M on the $175M raised proxy. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces a $1.0B midpoint valuation, with a $300M floor and $3.0B ceiling (Dream Security at the high end).

The triangulated valuation range spans $283M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $666M. The wide spread reflects material dispersion in the peer set—a 10x range from minimum to maximum valuation. Key uncertainties include relative competitive positioning within terahertz sensing, revenue traction versus peer-comparable milestones, and customer concentration in defense procurement (a sector with extended sales cycles). Stage-progression yields a conservative floor; peer multiples suggest material upside if technology and go-to-market execution track within sector norms.
